name: drag_path
title: Drag Path
description: Press a mouse button at the first observed image point, move through each following point of the same image in order and release, using a single-use proof from capture (pass target) or display_capture (pass display). Every point must lie inside the captured image (and window). Movement time is split across segments in proportion to their length. The button is released on every error path, including fail-safe trips mid-path. Checks the proof binding, freshness, display, cursor, cancellation and exact pixels in a clipped 32x32 patch at the start and end points before input; window proofs also check target identity, foreground and bounds. Does not activate a lost-focus window. Every attempt consumes the proof. Capture again to verify the result.

target.description: Window target of the latest capture. Supply exactly one of target or display, matching how the proof was taken.

display.description: Display reference of the latest display_capture. Supply exactly one of target or display.

capture_id.description: Unused capture_id returned by capture or display_capture in this connection, valid for 60 seconds.

points.description: Path points in order, relative to the captured image top-left corner.

x.description: Pixel x, relative to the captured image left edge.

y.description: Pixel y, relative to the captured image top edge.

duration_ms.description: Total movement time while the button is held, split across segments by length.

target.description: Window target the capture was bound to, if any.

display.description: Display reference the capture was bound to, if any.

x.description: Screen x the input started at (desktop physical pixels).

y.description: Screen y the input started at (desktop physical pixels).

note.description: What happened and how to verify it.

dragged.description: True when the drag path completed.

points_sent.description: Number of path points traversed, including the start.

to.description: Final path point in desktop physical pixels.

name: paste_text
title: Paste Text
description: Activate target, put text on the clipboard, press Ctrl+V in the focused control and, by default, restore the previous clipboard text afterwards. Rechecks foreground and cancellation before the paste. Only text clipboard contents are restored; a non-text clipboard is not restored and the note says so. Clipboard contents are visible to other applications while the text is there. Confirm the result by capturing the app.

target.description: Session target from the latest windows_list. Re-list invalidates previous targets.

text.description: Text to paste; no shell evaluation

restore_clipboard.description: Restore the previous clipboard text after the paste settles (150 ms).

clipboard_restored.description: True when the previous clipboard text was put back.

note.description: How to verify the result, and whether the clipboard was restored.
